raw_response:
I will still do the same wheat-maize cycle on all 9 mu. That is what I know, and on our side in Quzhou this system is steady if water is there. I have well irrigation, so I will not farm too lightly on fertilizer. Fertilizer costs money, but if I save too much and the yield drops, that loss is bigger. I have farmed 40 years, and I do not start from zero every year. I look at what I used last year, then I adjust a little by the stand, the soil strength, and what I saw in nearby fields. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put more fertilizer at the base, then add urea at jointing. Wheat here answers well to water, so I will water about three times if the season is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed. Hybrid maize costs more, but the ears are more even and the yield is steadier, so I will spend that money. I will not use too little nitrogen on maize, because if the seedlings look weak later, it is hard to catch back up. On my 9 mu, family labor is not enough for everything at peak time, so I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage after each harvest. I will spray when needed, mainly herbicide once and then one or two more pesticide sprays depending on insects and disease. If the weather is normal and water is available, I will aim for a solid wheat crop and a stronger maize crop.

I will stay close to last year’s practice and not cut fertilizer too much, because losing yield costs more than wasting a little fertilizer. For wheat I will use improved seed, base fertilizer plus one nitrogen topdressing, and about three irrigations in a normal year. For maize I will use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen a bit heavier than wheat, and water two times if rainfall is not enough.
